title: Canary timing & stakeholder calendar — scratchpad
content:
Purpose:
This is a working scratchpad for coordinating canary timing, stakeholder notification windows, and a lightweight cross-functional calendar for LLM feature rollouts. Goal: reduce surprise, align on windows that respect business cycles, avoid noisy telemetry during peak traffic, and make canaries predictable for SRE/Oncall, Product, and CS.

Scope:
- Applies to feature changes that touch inference behavior (model changes, routing changes, caching/kv updates, prompt-layer updates, cost-modeling switches like quantization), as well as control-plane changes that affect routing/exposure.
- Not for purely UI cosmetic changes unless they change request patterns.

Quick principles (heuristics):
- Golden window: run canaries 48–72 hours after low-traffic weekday midnight local-region windows when possible. Why: signal-to-noise ratio for latency and error-rate metrics improves overnight; CS/product availability is still possible.
- Minimum observation: 24 hours of steady state after each exposure increment (longer for A/B with user behaviour metrics).
- Exposure ramp: 0% -> 0.1% -> 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 100%. Minimum time at each step: 24h (0.1%/1% can be shorter if synthetic traffic verifies correctness).
- Sizing slices: prefer stable cohorts (e.g., platform-internal traffic, internal beta users, small subset of customers) instead of random sampling for first two steps.
- Rolling windows: avoid starting a new step within 6 hours of any scheduled maintenance on infra or major marketing events.

Stakeholder notification matrix (who needs to know and when):
- T-minus planning (>= 7 days): Product PM (owner), Eng TL, SRE lead, Solutions Eng, Customer Success lead, Legal (if compliance change), Growth (if potential marketing impact).
- T-minus 2 days: Ops runbook distributed, Canary schedule + Zoom link published, oncall rotation confirmed, test checklist sign-off by Eng/QA.
- T-minus 2 hours: Reminder to primary oncall, product steward, and CS.
- Post-increment immediate (0–15m): Commit message + brief in #rollouts channel with exposure % and telemetry pointers.
- Post-increment 24h: Short write-up to stakeholders with top-line signals (latency, p50/p95, error rates, cost delta, quality regression metrics if available).

Telemetry gating (pass/fail heuristics) — initial guardrails:
- Latency: p95 increase > 20% relative to baseline over last 7 days => FAIL for that step.
- Errors: 5xx spike > 3x baseline rate or absolute increase > 0.1% => FAIL.
- Quality regressions: automated eval set score drop > 2% absolute (or configured threshold per model/feature) => FAIL.
- Cost: token-unit cost increase > 25% per request at scale => REVIEW (not automatic FAIL if tradeoff approved).
- User impact signals: CS complaint volume from canary cohort > 2 tickets in first 24h => REVIEW.
- Telemetry window: evaluate using rolling 60m windows with anomaly detection, but require human confirmation for fail decisions.

Primary runbook checklist (dry run before canary):
- [ ] Confirm baseline snapshot (metrics dashboard saved: latency, errors, cost, quality evals).
- [ ] Synthetic smoke tests (1000 requests through canary routing, measure correctness and latency).
- [ ] Canary config validated in Staging infra and export of traffic partition rules.
- [ ] Oncall rota & escalation phone tree published.
- [ ] Contact matrix for customer-impacting customers (Solution Eng has list).
- [ ] Rehearsal: 30-minute dry-run with SRE/Product walking through rollback steps and communication templates.
- [ ] Postmortem template pre-created in Jira/Confluence if the release goes into incident mode.

Rollback & fallback options (fast and safe):
1) Traffic re-route to previous model variant (preferred) — immediate with automated fallback route.
2) Scale down exposure to last safe step (e.g., from 5% back to 1%).
3) Circuit-breaker: route affected endpoints to slower but more conservative routing path (dedicated tier vs. burst).
4) Deactivate feature flag server-side if the change is feature-flagged.

Cross-functional calendar (6-week sample for a major model/prompt rollout) — owner = Product PM
Week -2 (prep):
- Mon: Kickoff with Eng/SRE/Solutions/CS (1h). Draft runbook.
- Wed: Synthetic test pass + sign-off.
- Fri: Stakeholder alignment sync: refine calendar + customer impact list.
Week -1 (rehearsal):
- Tue: Ops rehearsal + smoke tests. Publish rollback procedures.
- Thu: Legal/Privacy review complete if needed.
Week 0 (canary week):
- Mon 00:00 local region: start 0.1% internal-only slice (watch 12–48h).
- Wed: move to 1% customer-slice if no fails.
- Fri: expand to 5% if prior windows healthy.
Week 1 (stabilize):
- Tue: expand to 20% if all signals green.
- Thu: full release candidate.
Week 2–3 (monitor):
- Ongoing weekly syncs (Mon): primaries share signal postcards; CS monitors ticketing.
Week 4–6 (retrospective + tuning):
- Collect quality regressions, cost analysis, and postmortem if required.

Meeting cadence templates (short):
- Daily quick-check (15m) during active canary window — attendees: Product PM, SRE rep, Oncall, Solutions Eng.
- Weekly summary (30m) — extended stakeholders, includes GTM/Growth if rollout affects UX/metrics.

Communication templates (in-channel snippets):
- Start of step: "Canary step started: exposure 1%, model vX. Observability dashboard: <link>. Oncall: @sre_oncall. Please do not schedule infra maintenance for next 24h."
- Fail announcement: "Canary failed step X at T. Immediate action: rollback to vY executed. Postmortem ticket: JIRA-RW-XXXX. Brief: latency p95 up 35% + eval drop 3% on eval-set."

Edge cases / advices from prior experiments (notes to self):
- Don’t iterate canary increments faster than the telemetry window allows — false positives from short windows cause unnecessary rollbacks.
- Use deterministic internal cohorts first — they are high signal for correctness issues that customer sampling can dilute.
- For reranking/embedding changes, user-visible KPIs may take longer to show (search CTR, relevance) — extend the 24h minimum to 7–14 days for those metrics.
- Coordinate with billing/finance if a rollout changes per-token cost expectations for paid customers; sometimes we need proactive comms.

Open questions / discussion points:
- What is our canonical internal cohort definition? (Priya to confirm list + how to create a persistent cookie-based cohort).
- How to automate gating for quality regressions where human judgement is needed (tradeoff classifier + review flow?).
- Should we add a separate calendar track for enterprise customers where we can opt them in/out of canaries? (Sofia + Solutions Eng to propose).

Next steps (short):
- Omar: build a template calendar ICS that can be reused by PMs (due EOW).
- Priya: finalize internal cohort list + share how to wire in traffic partition rules (due 2026-03-17).
- Maya (owner): schedule a 30min rehearsal with SRE & oncall next Tue.

Appendix: quick links + artifacts to attach to any canary kickoff:
- Baseline dashboard snapshot (link)
- Synthetic smoke suite report (attach)
- Rehearsal recording + notes
- Customer-impact list (Solutions Eng doc)
- Runbook checklist (this doc)
